Guitar / Pentatonic

Make music with five notes.

A minor pentatonic uses A C D E G. Learn a small area first, then turn it into a phrase.

Try it on the fretboard ↗

Understand

The formula is 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7. A is the root: the pink notes show where a phrase can feel settled. The diagram shows only notes inside the displayed fret window.

Standard tuning: E A D G B E, from the thickest string to the thinnest.

Play it

Play A–C–D, pause, then E–G–A. Use the next A available on your strings. Repeat the phrase backwards without speeding up.

Listen and check

Leave a beat of silence between phrases. Finish first on C, then on A: listen to the different feeling of resolution. C major pentatonic shares these notes but has C as its centre.

Choose a lesson

Fretboard notes ↗

A fret is one semitone. The same note appears in several places: use the open strings and the 12th fret as landmarks.

Triads ↗

A triad contains a root, a third and a fifth. The three shapes below contain the same A minor notes: A C E.

Chords ↗

Choose a root and a chord type. Compare open, barre and compact shapes, then use a position that suits the song and your hand.

Daily routine ↗

Keep A minor as your reference and connect notes, pentatonic phrases, triads and rhythm.
